F6 carried-position carry with a qualifying tie RRS A8 cannot break: both boats carry the shared position and the next position is skipped

470 (and classes using the same carried-position wording) 2026 — European Championship · F6 · D11 · SI (Typical wording — see notes) · results (n/a — constructed to isolate the tie)

2 qualifying fleets · → Gold/Silver · discards: 1 discard from race 3.
The carried-position wording — "The position of each boat in the Qualifying
Series shall be carried forward to the Final Series as non excludable
points" — has no tie clause of its own, so the qualifying ranking is RRS A8
as written. A tie A8 cannot break therefore leaves two boats genuinely
holding one position, and the position of each boat is the same number:
both carry it, and no boat carries the position skipped past.

y1 and b1 each win both qualifying races of their own fleets — identical
score lists in different fleets, which A8.1 compares equal and the A8.2
count-back walks through without separating. They are joint 1st, both
carry 1 point, and nobody carries 2. Alongside them, b2 (2,3) and b3 (3,2)
tie on 5 but the count-back's last race breaks them, so their carried
positions stay distinct — 5 and 4.

Hand-verification (fleets of 3; two qualifying races, below the three-race
discard threshold, so nothing is dropped):

Qualifying totals:
  y1 1+1=2   y2 2+2=4   y3 3+3=6 | b1 1+1=2   b2 2+3=5   b3 3+2=5
Qualifying positions: 1 y1, 1 b1, 3 y2, 4 b3, 5 b2, 6 y3.
Split into equal blocks: Gold y1/b1/y2, Silver b3/b2/y3.

Each boat carries that position (the QS column) and sails two final races
— two *races*, short of the three-race threshold, so still no discard:

  y1 1 + 1,2 = 4   b1 1 + 2,1 = 4   y2 3 + 3,3 = 9
  b3 4 + 1,2 = 7   b2 5 + 2,1 = 8   y3 6 + 3,3 = 12

The equal carried points leave y1 and b1 still level on 4 — and now the
final series can do what the qualifying series could not: A8.1 compares
[1,1,2] against [1,1,2] equal, and the count-back's last race (y1 2, b1 1)
puts b1 ahead. The tie was carried faithfully, not decided by the carry.
